t.6.83.1: In Laṅkā, in house after house, Rāvaṇa heard the piteous cry and lamentation of the grief-stricken rākṣasī women.
t.6.83.2: But Rāvaṇa, sighing deeply and remaining absorbed in thought for a moment, became exceedingly enraged and terrible to behold.
t.6.83.3: Biting his lip with his teeth, his eyes reddened with fury, he was hard to look upon even for the Rākṣasas, like the fire of universal destruction blazing up.
t.6.83.4: And there the lord of the rākṣasas spoke to the rākṣasas standing near him, whose speech had become indistinct through fear, as though he were burning them up with his eyes.
t.6.83.5: Quickly tell Mahodara, Mahāpārśva, the rākṣasa Virūpākṣa, and the troops: 'March out at my command!'
t.6.83.6: Hearing those words of his, those rākṣasas, tormented by fear, urged on the steady rākṣasas by the king's command.
t.6.83.7: All those fearsome-looking rākṣasas said, "So be it," and, having had rites for their welfare performed, they all went forth toward Rāvaṇa.
t.6.83.8: Having duly honored Rāvaṇa as was fitting, all those great chariot-warriors stood with joined palms, longing for the victory of their master.
t.6.83.9: Then Rāvaṇa, overwhelmed with rage, laughed and spoke to them, to Mahodara and Mahāpārśva and to the rākṣasa Virūpākṣa.
t.6.83.10: Today, with arrows loosed from my bow, blazing like the sun at the end of the age, I shall send Rāghava and Lakṣmaṇa to the abode of Yama.
t.6.83.11: Today, by slaying my enemy, I shall exact requital for Khara, for Kumbhakarṇa, and likewise for Prahasta and Indrajit.
t.6.83.12: I shall see to it that neither the sky, nor the quarters, nor the rivers, nor even the ocean come to light, shrouded as they will be by the clouds of my arrows.
t.6.83.13: Today, with waves of arrows rising from the ocean of my bow, I shall churn, troop by troop, those hosts of the leaders of the monkey bands.
t.6.83.14: Today, like an elephant, I shall churn up the lakes that are the troops of those who gleam like lotus filaments, lakes thick with clusters of full-blown lotuses.
t.6.83.15: Today in battle the leaders of the monkey troops, their faces pierced with arrows, will adorn the earth as if with lotuses still on their stalks.
t.6.83.16: Today in battle, with a single arrow loosed, I shall pierce the monkeys, fierce in combat and fighting with trees, by hundreds upon hundreds.
t.6.83.17: Those women whose husband has been slain, whose brother has been slain, and whose sons have been slain, today, by slaying the enemy, I shall wipe away their tears.
t.6.83.18: Today in battle, with monkeys split open by my arrows, strewn about and lifeless, I shall cover the earth so thickly that its surface can be glimpsed only with effort.
t.6.83.19: Today the jackals, the vultures, and all the other eaters of flesh, all of them I shall satisfy with the flesh of my enemies, torn by my arrows.
t.6.83.20: Let my chariot be made ready at once, and let my bow be brought quickly! Let the night-rangers who remain follow me into battle.
t.6.83.21: Hearing those words of his, Mahāpārśva spoke to the army commanders standing there: "Let the army be hastened!"
t.6.83.22: Then the army commanders, agitated and swift in their movements, went all around Laṅkā, urging those rākṣasas on from house to house.
t.6.83.23: Then, after a moment, the Rākṣasas of terrible prowess and fearsome faces rushed forth, roaring, with arms bearing various weapons.
t.6.83.24: With swords, paṭṭisas, tridents, maces, pestles and ploughshares, with sharp-edged spears and with huge war-hammers…
t.6.83.25: With staves, with gleaming discuses and sharpened axes, with bhiṇḍipālas, with śataghnīs, and with other excellent weapons as well.
t.6.83.26: Then, at Rāvaṇa's command, four commanders of the army swiftly brought up a chariot furnished with a charioteer and yoked with eight horses.
t.6.83.27: Rāvaṇa mounted his divine chariot, blazing with its own splendor, as if splitting the earth apart by the sheer weight of his mighty being.
t.6.83.28: Then Mahāpārśva and Mahodara, permitted by Rāvaṇa, and the invincible Virūpākṣa mounted their chariots.
t.6.83.29: But they, thrilled with joy and roaring loudly, as though splitting the earth, sallied forth eager for victory, letting loose a terrible cry.
t.6.83.30: Then the splendid one, surrounded by the hosts and forces of the rākṣasas, went forth to battle with his bow raised, like Kāla, Antaka and Yama.
t.6.83.31: Then that great chariot-warrior, in a chariot drawn by swift horses, went out through that gate where the two, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, were.
t.6.83.32: Then the sun lost its radiance and the quarters were shrouded in darkness; fearsome birds cried out, and the earth trembled.
t.6.83.33: The god of rain poured down blood, and the horses stumbled; a vulture alighted on the top of the banner, and jackals howled inauspiciously.
t.6.83.34: His left eye throbbed and his left arm trembled; his face lost its color, and his voice faltered somewhat.
t.6.83.35: Then, as the rākṣasa Daśagrīva sallied forth to the fight, these portents foretelling his death in battle were seen.
t.6.83.36: From the sky a meteor fell with a sound like a thunderclap; vultures shrieked inauspiciously, answered in turn by crows.
t.6.83.37: Paying no heed to these dreadful portents that had appeared, Rāvaṇa, out of delusion, sallied forth bent on slaughter, driven on by Time.
t.6.83.38: But at the rumbling of the chariots of those mighty-souled rākṣasas, the army of the vānaras also advanced, intent on battle alone.
t.6.83.39: A most tumultuous battle took place between those monkeys and rākṣasas, who, enraged and eager for victory, challenged one another.
t.6.83.40: Then Daśagrīva, enraged, wrought great slaughter among the ranks of the vānaras with his arrows adorned with gold.
t.6.83.41: Some of the monkeys had their heads cut off by Rāvaṇa; some were slain, left without breath; some were torn open at the flanks; some had their heads shattered, and some were deprived of their eyes.
t.6.83.42: Wherever Daśānana, his eyes rolling with rage, advanced upon his chariot in battle, there those leaders of the monkey troops could not withstand the force of his arrows.
